newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK short cash, short-end govt papers yield higher.
newsitem.headline: HK short cash, short-end govt papers yield higher.

text.p: Yields on Hong Kong short cash and short-end government paper gained on Thursday on tightened Hong Kong dollar liquidity, dealers said.
Overnight cash rates firmed to 5-1/4 3/16 from 5-3/16 1/16 at the Wednesday midsession on hot demand for Hong Kong dollars.
The Hong Kong Monetary Authority, the de facto central bank, injected about HK$100 million into the money market, but dealers said the move had only limited impact on cash rates.
A European bank dealer said the rates had been buoyed by offers from some big players towards the end of the session.
Three-month rates were steady at 5-1/2 15/32 percent versus 5-9/16 7/16.

Yields on one-week Exchange Fund bills rose to 4.87 percent versus 4.80, tracking the rises in short cash rates, dealers said. Yields on long-end government papers were lower in line with U.S. Treasuries, they said.
Seven-year Exchange Fund notes yielded 7.30 percent versus 7.32. Yields of five-year notes eased to 6.94 from 6.96 percent, and yields of three-year notes to 6.36 from 6.40 percent.
